labour_shares.source: Penn World Table 11.0, labsh, via FRED
labour_shares.units_input: Annual ratio, at current national prices, not seasonally adjusted.
labour_shares.units_plot: Percent of GDP. Compensation includes the estimated labour income of self-employed workers.
labour_shares.transformation: Multiply by 100; no smoothing or interpolation; retain missing observations as gaps.
labour_shares.interpretation: Descriptive historical series, not a causal estimate of automation or generative AI.

computer_income_share.source: C. Jones and Tonetti (May 2026), Figure 2, printed page 14, PDF page 15; BLS (2024).
computer_income_share.units: Share of private business value added paid to IT capital, percent; not purchases of computers, investment/GDP, technology-company profits, or all capital income.
computer_income_share.transformation: Manually transcribed rounded endpoints, approximately 4.3% in 2000 and 3.0% in 2023. Not an annual series; no interpolation.
computer_income_share.vintage: Historical evidence as reported in the May 2026 working paper; not a claim about the post-2023 AI boom.

theory.conditions: Strong complementarity across tasks (elasticity below one), fixed task allocation for the better-machine comparative static. Not every worker benefits; labour-share changes and wage changes are distinct.

refresh_command: python -c "import figures_s3 as f; f.refresh_ai_distribution_evidence(); f.ai_computer_income_share(); f.ai_labour_shares()"
